papers.title: Generic Inference in Latent Gaussian Process Models
papers.abstract: We develop an automated variational method for inference in models with Gaussian process (GP) priors and general likelihoods. The method supports multiple outputs and multiple latent functions and does not require detailed knowledge of the conditional likelihood, only needing its evaluation as a black-box function. Using a mixture of Gaussians as the variational distribution, we show that the evidence lower bound and its gradients can be estimated efficiently using samples from univariate Gaussian distributions. Furthermore, the method is scalable to large datasets which is achieved by using an augmented prior via the inducing-variable approach underpinning most sparse GP approximations, along with parallel computation and stochastic optimization. We evaluate our approach quantitatively and qualitatively with experiments on small datasets, medium-scale datasets and large datasets, showing its competitiveness under different likelihood models and sparsity levels. On the large-scale experiments involving prediction of airline delays and classification of handwritten digits, we show that our method is on par with the state-of-the-art hard-coded approaches for scalable GP regression and classification.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了高斯过程模型的通用推断方法，但未涉及代理模型在有限元分析或生物力学设计中的应用。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address surrogate modelling for expensive simulations, does not handle constraints or uncertainty quantification in engineering design, and lacks validation on physical or biomechanical systems.

summary_zh.motivation: 自动化高斯过程模型在一般似然函数下的变分推断。
summary_zh.method: 使用高斯混合变分分布和诱导变量实现可扩展推断。
summary_zh.result: 在小到大数据集上取得与专用方法竞争的结果。
summary_zh.validation: 在标准机器学习基准上验证预测误差和分类准确率。

summary_en.motivation: Develop an automated variational inference method for Gaussian process models with general black-box likelihoods.
summary_en.method: Propose a mixture of Gaussians variational distribution combined with inducing variables for scalable inference and optimization.
summary_en.result: Achieve competitive performance on small to large-scale datasets compared to hand-crafted approaches.
summary_en.validation: Evaluate on benchmark regression and classification tasks including airline delays and digit recognition.

papers.title: Microstructure and strength analysis of eutectic Al-Si alloy in-situ manufactured using selective laser melting from elemental powder mixture
papers.first_author_affiliation: University Bourgogne Franche-Comte, IRTES EA7274, F-90100, Belfort, France

corresponding_authors.name: Nan Kang
corresponding_authors.affiliation: University Bourgogne Franche-Comte, IRTES EA7274, F-90100, Belfort, France

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文主要研究铝硅合金的选区激光熔化制造，与生物医学植入物材料（如钛合金）无关，未涉及多孔结构、应力遮挡或骨整合。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not use a biomedical implant material, does not create porous structures for stress shielding, does not perform fatigue testing, and does not report surface roughness or osseointegration.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究铝硅合金激光熔化制造的微观结构与强度。
summary_zh.method: 使用元素粉末混合物进行选区激光熔化制造。
summary_zh.result: 获得了细小的共晶组织和高强度。
summary_zh.validation: 通过微观组织观察和力学性能测试验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the microstructure and strength of eutectic Al-Si alloy fabricated by selective laser melting from elemental powders.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting was used to in-situ manufacture the alloy from a mixture of aluminum and silicon powders.
summary_en.result: The as-built alloy exhibited a fine eutectic microstructure and high compressive strength.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through microstructural characterization and mechanical testing.

papers.title: Mechanical testing of a selective laser melted superalloy
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting is an additive manufacturing technology where metal powder is melted by a laser source layer-wise, forming a solid, dense metallic component. With the selective laser meting process, near net shape components can be manufactured directly from a 3D-model. The model is sliced into thin layers and a powder is spread onto a build platform. In the next step, the powder is fused by a laser as dictated by the model. The laser energy is intense enough to permit full melting (welding) of the particles to form solid metal. The process is repeated layer by layer until the part is complete. A number of materials are available, including steel, aluminium, titanium and, in recent time, also superalloys. The material investigated in the current project is a nickel base superalloy composition-wise equivalent to Hastelloy X, a solution strengthened superalloy typically used in large welded components exposed to high temperatures in oxidizing as well as reducing environments. Microstructurally, the material is different from both a hot-rolled, as well as a cast material due to the manufacturing process. Since the SLM process involves laser melting of powder particles in the size range of &lt;50μm, the structure resembles of a weld structure, however on a smaller scale. Due to the layer-by-layer build strategy, the material will exhibit anisotropy. In the current project, high temperature mechanical fatigue and creep tests are performed. The microstructure is evaluated and the influence on the mechanical properties is discussed. Anisotropy in mechanical properties is discussed and the underlying factors of the anisotropy are analyzed.

summary_zh.method: 对Hastelloy X合金进行SLM成型，开展高温疲劳和蠕变测试
summary_zh.result: 发现微观结构类似焊缝，力学性能存在各向异性
summary_zh.validation: 通过高温力学实验验证性能差异

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the mechanical anisotropy of a nickel-base superalloy fabricated by selective laser melting for high-temperature applications.
summary_en.method: Hastelloy X specimens were produced via SLM and subjected to high-temperature fatigue and creep tests.
summary_en.result: The material exhibited a weld-like microstructure and significant anisotropy in mechanical properties.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing under high-temperature conditions was used to characterize performance.
